# Results — Study 277 (Trading-Cards) vs the S&P 500

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The graded-card index
is curated and hardcoded in [`data.py`](../trading_cards/data.py) (base 100 = 1990).
S&P 500 calendar-year **price** returns are from the cached `^GSPC_split_only.parquet`
(repo-level cache, read-only). Match the fingerprints below to confirm you hold the
same data. As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n paired years | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| Curated graded-card price index | 1990–2025 (returns 1991–2025) | 35 | `card_return = 557588f16e2e` |
| S&P 500 (^GSPC, nominal price, Dec/Dec) | 1991–2025 | 35 | `gspc_return = 2e653d757b43` |

Both series are **price-only** (no dividends; cards pay no yield). Adding S&P
dividends widens the equity lead — the comparison here is deliberately the one
most favourable to cards.

## Return & risk — cards lose on every axis

| Metric | Cards | S&P 500 (price) |
|---|--:|--:|
| CAGR | **+5.2%/yr** | **+9.0%/yr** |
| Annualised vol | 18.7% | 17.0% |
| Sharpe (rf = 0) | **0.35** | **0.62** |
| Max drawdown | **−44.1%** | −40.1% |

Cards compounded slower, at *higher* volatility, with a *deeper* drawdown. There
is no risk-adjusted edge.

## Structural alpha over equity beta (Newey-West HAC, 2 lags)

Model: `card_t = α + β · gspc_t + ε_t`.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| α (gross) | **+3.42%/yr** |
| HAC t(α) | **1.331** |
| p(α) | 0.183 |
| β | 0.29 |
| Correlation | +0.263 |
| R² | 0.069 |

The point estimate of alpha is positive but the **HAC t-stat is 1.33 — below the
|t| ≥ 2 bar** this desk requires for a REAL signal. Beta is low (0.29), which is
the entire diversification pitch, but a low-beta sleeve with an insignificant,
fragile alpha is not an edge — especially before costs.

## After collectible frictions (~15% one-way, amortised over a 5-year hold)

A round trip costs `2 × 15% = 30%`, amortised over 5 years ≈ 6%/yr drag.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| Net card CAGR | **−0.9%/yr** |
| Net alpha | **−2.58%/yr** (HAC t = −1.01) |

The already-insignificant gross alpha goes **negative** after realistic frictions.
The asset class loses money once you pay the auction and grading toll.

## Block bootstrap (gross alpha, stationary block = 3, 5000 reps)

| Percentile | Alpha (%/yr) |
|---|--:|
| 2.5% | −1.81 |
| 50% | +3.44 |
| 97.5% | +8.99 |
| Fraction > 0 | 91% |

The 95% CI **includes zero**, so even gross the alpha is not reliably positive.

## The one-boom fragility

The entire outperformance is the 2020–2021 mania:

| Sub-period | Cards CAGR | S&P CAGR |
|---|--:|--:|
| 1991–2014 (long grind) | +3.2%/yr | +7.9%/yr |
| 2015–2021 (boom) | **+23.4%/yr** | +12.7%/yr |
| 2022–2025 (bust) | **−10.9%/yr** | +9.5%/yr |

Cards beat stocks in exactly **one** window. Dropping just 2020 and 2021, the card
index compounds at **+2.1%/yr** — below cash, before costs.

## Diversification check — the hedge failed when needed

Full-sample correlation to equities is a modest **+0.26**, the basis of the
diversification claim. But in the **2022** risk-off the card index fell **−30%**
versus the S&P's **−19%** — cards fell *harder* than stocks exactly when a hedge
was supposed to help.

## Honesty checks

- **Execution lag / settlement:** an asset-class comparison uses contemporaneous
  calendar-year levels, but the *trade* settles weeks later via auction — modelled
  as the friction drag above, not as a return lag.
- **One-way costs × NAV:** 15% one-way (auction premium + grading), round trip
  amortised over a 5-year hold. Shorts are not applicable — you cannot borrow a
  Charizard, so there is no short-side leg and no borrow cost.
- **Gross/net and price/total-return labelled:** card index is price-only; S&P is
  price-only to match; total-return equities would win by more.
- **Survivorship named on the Signal axis:** the curated index, like every
  collectible index, tracks cards that kept trading, biasing it *upward*.
- **Synthetic cells** in the notebooks are clearly fenced behind `HAVE_REAL` and
  never presented under a real-tape banner.

## Positive control

The synthetic paired generator plants a structural card alpha; the Newey-West test
clears |t| ≥ 2 once the planted premium and sample size are large enough — so the
null result is about the **asset class and its costs**, not the method.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Cards underperformed equities on CAGR (5.2% vs 9.0%) and
  Sharpe (0.35 vs 0.62) with a deeper drawdown; the structural alpha's HAC t-stat
  is 1.33 (< 2) and the bootstrap CI includes zero. The index is survivorship-biased
  upward, so the true edge is, if anything, worse.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net of realistic, amortised frictions the CAGR is
  **negative**; there is no liquid, low-cost vehicle, and the modest correlation
  bought no hedge in 2022.
- **Busted — a single boom in a trench coat.** The whole "cards beat stocks" story
  is the 2020–2021 mania, which fully round-tripped; ex-boom the index compounds at
  2.1%/yr.
